2.why: src/MentalMasterClock.cpp:188, five times a square that swings between -1 and 1

comment: Index order is not panel order: the enum runs BEAT, EIGHTHS, SIXTEENTHS, BAR while the widget draws Beat, Bar, 8ths and 16ths down the panel (src/MentalMasterClock.cpp:282-285); the tags are written from the widget. The bottom of the time signature is stored 0 to 3 and raised as two to the power of that plus one, giving 2, 4, 8 and 16 (line 134), but only the branches for 4 and for 8 set the clock frequency and the counter limits (lines 164-184), so 2 and 16 leave them where they were. The module has no clock input and no reset input: the reset is a button only, and it is read as a level rather than as an edge (line 137), so it holds rather than fires. The run state is saved with the patch and the module comes up running when there is nothing saved (line 68). The panel prints Master Clock, Tempo, Run, Reset, Beat, Bar, 8ths and 16ths.
